html:
Konolkhatep (F66) campaign chain

Region in the English rating survey: Sarhal.

Starting country: Gnollakaz (U09) Formable country: Konolkhatep (F66)

In one sentence: Begin with Grizaka's gnoll conquerors, seize the Stewardship of the Sorrow, and remake Kheterata as a world empire sustained by gnolls, Khetism, slave-driven projects and a god-king. Both its story and mechanics are exceptionally rich, but it demands intensive expansion, tolerance for dark themes and patience with a long endgame.

Story: exceptionally rich | Mission-tree length: exceptionally long (9 U09 missions and 56 F66 missions, 65 direct missions in total) | Mission-tree currency: checked against local v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: exceptionally high | Grind: very high | Early pressure: high | Expansion capacity: exceptionally high

Identity and history

Konolkhatep (F66) is not a starting country in 1444. Its clearest playable formation route starts as Gnollakaz (U09); this does not mean every campaign or setting version gives it the same foundation year. Gnollakaz is a Pyreclaw gnoll state west of the Sorrow, following the Xhazobkult and ruled by Grizaka, the Empress-of-Gnollkind. [Local history scripts; official development diary]

Before 1444, Grizaka has already united the Pyreclaw packs, dealt Kheterata a severe blow and identified Viakkoc as her rival. Her attributes and Conqueror/Tactical Genius traits give the route a strongly personal heroic character: rather than slowly developing a peripheral tribe, you are turning an already successful invasion into a new empire. [Local history scripts]

The offline Wiki gives a more detailed account: Grizaka united the Pyreclaws in 1438, marched east in 1439 and killed Viakkoc IX outside Kheterat in 1442. The Pyreclaw article also says the Kheteratan army subsequently repulsed her and her daughter Izhrukt completed the conquest in the sixteenth century. The Kingdom of Kheterata article instead attributes the kingdom's conquest to Grizaka herself. Neither account is therefore presented here as an undisputed F66 foundation chronology. Grizaka retained local human administration and freedom of worship in conquered lands, while brutal mine slavery financed her wars. This helps explain the later combination of institutional incorporation and an enslaving empire. [Wiki; source conflict]

National story and campaign arc

Gnollakaz's short tree is the prologue to the full campaign: conquer the Sorrow, seize Stewardship authority, establish a professional army and demonstrate Grizaka's imperial credentials. After the key mission, the player can change Tag to Konolkhatep. Other eligible gnolls can also form it by decision after satisfying culture, Stewardship and territorial requirements. [Local missions; formation decision]

The defining change is not a new flag but the abandonment of the Xhazobkult for Khetism and Kheterata's imperial inheritance. Conquest no longer relies solely on pack organisation and demon worship: human bureaucrats, Medasi subjects, Stewardship and gnollish rule by the strong become parts of a new order. [Local scripts; official development diary]

Core mechanics

The Steward's empire and human integration. The formed state's template uses monarchy, Sorrowmane gnoll culture and Elikhetist religion. Missions ask you to placate the Khet, integrate Kheteratan humans and expand through Mandate, Stewardship reforms and Medasi/satrapy subjects. This is not simply an extermination route, but an imperial fusion imposed by its conquerors. [Local history; missions]

Slaves and major projects. Its government mechanic stores 0–1000 slaves, with faster monthly attrition at higher stocks. Slaves can be obtained through trade, ports, subjects, coastal raiding, peace treaties and other channels, then spent on roads, pyramids, temples and statues. This is the main connection between the economy, war and expansion—and the darkest institutional core of the campaign. [Local government mechanic; localisation]

Five Kheteratan legions. Missions unlock five elite legions. They can fight as high-quality mercenaries and provide nationwide modifiers when not hired. Each costs substantial manpower, money and slaves to establish, making them both a major power spike and expensive imperial projects. [Local missions; localisation]

The Last Great Fire and the god-king. A mid-campaign disaster, the Last Great Fire, advances more quickly under low Mandate and unintegrated gnoll cultures. During it the country suffers unrest, devastation, morale and reinforcement penalties and temporarily cannot declare war. The crisis directs the ruler towards Elikhet and divine power. The later tree centres on Horutep accumulating titles, sacred symbols and power on the road to immortality and apotheosis. [Local disaster; missions]

Gameplay by stage

Gnollakaz prologue: Use Grizaka's military strengths to subdue Kheterata and rival gnolls quickly, completing the nine preliminary missions. This is not merely a standalone short tree: it prepares territory, troops, Stewardship authority and permanent rewards for the formable country.

Formation and integration: After forming F66, stabilise Mandate, address human and gnoll integration and begin accumulating slaves and building projects. Expansion and disaster preparation must keep pace. Judging only by army strength while neglecting integration makes the mid-game crisis harder.

Legions and subjects: Establish the five legions and use satrapies, Medasi and tributaries to handle intercontinental expansion. Diplomacy here is not principally peaceful alliance-building: it determines which lands are governed directly and which operate as imperial dependencies.

God-king endgame: Once the central disaster is overcome, Horutep and the legions can usher in overwhelming military strength. The question increasingly becomes not whether you can win but whether you wish to finish the remaining conquests, cultural restructuring, subject organisation and project lists.

Mission futures and endgame

The tree's prospective future is for Konolkhatep to surpass old Kheterata: unite gnoll groups, control the Sorrow, expand its slave networks and projects, govern distant regions through legions and subjects, and transform Horutep from emperor into an eternal god-king. [Local missions]

No further successor Tag has been confirmed for this route. Its endgame transformation is internal: a conquering regime dependent on Grizaka's personal prestige becomes a dark world empire with durable institutions, global subjects, unique legions and an immortal ruler.

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 coordinates are expansion 95/100 | autocracy 95/100 | magic–artifice direction 85/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 85/100) | pluralism 15/100.

Its v2.1 values classification is Evil (9/100), with a stable trajectory. Slaves are counted as resources and consumed in major projects, legions and the ruler's apotheosis: institutional treatment of persons as instruments. The extent of conquest is not the principal reason for the low score.

Recommended for players who enjoy exceptionally long narrative trees, powerful warfare, subject management, distinctive resources and ascension after a major crisis. Avoid it if you dislike slavery narratives, only want peaceful development, resent late-game conquest checklists or do not want to read missions and events.

Community experience

[Community opinion] A help thread dated 2026-07-15 described the campaign as enjoyable and highly rewarding, arguing that the Last Great Fire is manageable if you prepare and read mission text. Replies emphasised assembling a large enough army and a buffer of Medasi beforehand.

[Community opinion] A late-game report dated 2026-08-05 praised the early missions and disaster, but warned that slowing expansion in the middle can produce pronounced fatigue from aggressive expansion, truce cycling, intercontinental warfare and subject conditions. This is player experience, not a script rule.

Evidence boundaries

The Chinese research concerns main Mod and localisation version v1.37.5.0, with a verification date of 2026-09-16. Its confirmation of Tags, names, U09→F66 formation, 65 direct missions, slaves, five legions, disaster and apotheosis is retained; this translation does not claim a fresh exhaustive audit.

The offline Wiki passages used are Gnollakaz (page_id=891, revision_id=29314), Pyreclaw Gnoll (3970/32025) and Kingdom of Kheterata (349/31421). The fall of Kheterata and Konolkhatep's inheritance around 1470 belong to the setting's future, not an inevitable player campaign. Design context comes from the cited Reddit development diaries; player opinions are limited to the two community threads.

There is also an ordinal discrepancy: the Pyreclaw Wiki passage says Viakkoc IX, whereas current Konolkhatep mission prose says Viakkoc X. The attribution above is retained rather than silently reconciled. Formation conditions do not resolve the disagreement between historical accounts.

See the original Chinese evidence record for full references and conflicts, and the English source-text receipt for the bounded English checks.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Konolkhatep (F66) — Konolkhatep Ideas

Applicable condition (alternative, not a stacked set):

    trigger = {
        tag = F66
    }

Traditions: Konolkhatepan Traditions

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +25%; Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 1: Of Khet & Gnolls

At first the relationship between the divine beings known as the Khet, and the gnolls of Konolkhatep was one of practicality, the Khet allowing the gnollish Emperors to maintain power and the gnolls facilitating the usual level of pampering the Khet were accustomed to. Over time the gnolls began to see in the Khet the expression of their ideals, these creatures lived in absolute luxury, never lifting a finger and being worshipped as gods. The gnollish nobility began to increasingly imitate the Khet themselves, constructing grand pleasure barges on which they sailed The Sorrow and maintaining vast coteries of servants and slaves to fulfil their every whim. In their own way, the gnolls became the greatest advocates the Khet had ever known.

Effects: Cat Mandate growth modifier: +0.05; Stability cost modifier: -10%.

Idea 2: Guardian of The Sorrow

While the human inhabitants of Kheterata had long argued and warred over the many interpretations of their Khetist faith the gnolls of Konolkhatep were less concerned with doctrinal differences and focused on the veneration and emulation of the Khet themselves. Though they might profess flexible loyalties to one sect or another over the centuries, the imperial household had an official policy of tolerance for all those who held the Khet to be sacred, adopting the gnollish style epithet of Guardian-of-The-Sorrow to mark their devotion to Khetism as a whole.

Effects: Tolerance of heretics: +3.

Idea 3: Feast of the Hostages

Just as the many minor rivers of central Sarhal flow into the mighty Sorrow, so goes the flow of tribute from the many lesser nations into mighty Konolkhatep. By taking hostage the firstborn children of the rulers of tributary states, the Emperors of Konolkhatep were able to ensure the flow of tribute remained consistent, whilst also preparing the neighbouring rulers of the future to continue this profitable relationship. Should the tributary states not uphold their side of the bargain, then the hostages would be ritually devoured by the Konolkhatepan royal family, their gnawed bones sent back to their parents as a warning of the price of disobedience.

Effects: Liberty desire from subject development: -0.25.

Idea 4: Gnollish Ahati

When the gnollish rulers first became Chosen of the Khet, they attempted to maintain many of the ancient traditions of Kheterata to appease their human subjects. Among these were the Ahati, the merchant-warriors that served as the warrior caste of the Kheteratan people. While the Ahati were traditionally a human institution, the growing population of gnolls throughout Kheterata soon began establishing their own brotherhoods. The rivalries between these traditional Ahati and the new Gnollish groups would spark an era of renewed militancy among the merchant warriors as they competed against one another for lucrative trading contracts, land rights and the favour of the imperial house.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 5: Heart of Sarhal

If the Sorrow is the lifeblood of Sarhal then Kheterata is undeniably it's heart. As Konolkhatep claimed more of the lands that had once belonged to the ancient empire they were forced to contend with peoples from many different cultures and ways of life. In order to keep such a disparate patchwork of people's living peacefully, the Emperors instituted an official edict of tolerance. It did not matter what language you spoke or what species you were, none of these would prevent your advancement within Konolkhatep. The only thing that mattered was loyalty to the Emperor and of course, the Khet.

Effects: Number of accepted cultures: +3.

Idea 6: Peace From The Mountains To The Sea

Throughout its history the lands of Kheterata have had to contend with gnollish raiders from outside its borders. With the establishment of Konolkhatep this came to an end, the gnollish dynasty subjugated the packs of the desert and brought an unprecedented era of peace and stability within the lands of Kheterata. A traveller could go from the mountains of Vus Mukis to the port of Koroshesh without fear of raiders, often seeing gnollish Ahati patrolling the highways and waterways of the empire. Merchants came to regard their deep red banners as a sign of safety and good fortune. This era of stability helped usher in a massive growth in the slave trade within central Sarhal as the gnoll packs that once captured and transported slaves were now firmly under the control of the Emperor, allowing merchants to focus on profit rather than protecting themselves from hostile packs and rival caravans.

Effects: Trade steering: +20%.

Idea 7: House of Golden Chains

Slavery had existed within Kheterata for centuries but the years of gnollish rulership brought a dramatic increase in the practice, though laws were issued that prohibited enslaving those classed as native Kheteratans, that being anyone born along The Sorrow and its tributaries. As a result many slaves were brought in from elsewhere in Sarhal. While most went on to the vast households of gnollish nobles, educated slaves or those that showed a talent for numbers were often sent to the House of Golden Chains.

The House of Golden Chains was an empire-wide organisation of slaves belonging to the Emperor who were employed solely to administer the vast territories of the empire. With no ties to the local areas they were stationed in and reliant on the state for their welfare, the Golden Chain slaves were thought to be less likely to embezzle funds than native bureaucrats and those that served the state well were often rewarded with a level of luxury beyond what even most free citizens were accustomed to.

Effects: Administrative efficiency: +5%.

Ambition: Konolkhatepan Ambition

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Gnollakaz (U09) — Gnollakaz Ideas

Applicable condition (alternative, not a stacked set):

    trigger = {
        tag = U09
    }

Traditions: Gnollakaz Traditions

Effects: Years of separatism: -5; Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 1: Victory on the Sorrow

In 1438 Pack Mistress Grizaka began her meteoric rise to power, unifying the Pyreclaw Gnolls and beginning an invasion of Irsmahapan that would split the Kheteratan empire in half, leading to the independence of the Tijarikheti states to the south. To the west, another gnollish power eyed Kheterata greedily, and soon the armies of Viakkoc marched to war along The Sorrow.

In 1442 the two gnollish states clashed outside of Kheterat. Even weakened by the siege of the city and outnumbered by their Seascourge foes, Grizaka’s military genius and use of shamanic fire magic saw the Pyreclaw victorious, slaughtering over half their enemies and causing a decisive rout. While Grizaka’s forces were eventually driven back by a Kheteratan counterattack, her victory over Viakkoc is still studied as a prime example of the importance of shock and awe tactics.

Effects: Land leader shock: +1.

Idea 2: Masters of Irsmahapan

Sandwiched between the Windhowlers to the west and the Pyreclaw to the east, the humans of Irsmahapan were used to dealing with gnollish raids, but the conquest of 1438 was unlike anything they had seen in centuries. Where many gnolls would have clapped the entire population in chains, Grizaka saw the wisdom of incorporating the existing power structures into her new empire. In return for supplying her forces with food, shelter and resources, the humans were allowed to continue worshipping their gods and were exempt from sacrificial tithes.

Effects: Tolerance of heathens: +2.

Idea 3: Empress of Gnollkind

When Grizaka drove the Viakkoc pack out of Kheterata it led to the downfall of their empire in West Sarhal. With the greatest pack of the age now defeated, Grizaka declared herself Empress-of-Gnollkind, seeking to claim the prestige and legitimacy of great states like Kheterata, Fangaula, the Phoenix Empire or distant Castanor. It was a powerful statement of her intent to unify the gnollish peoples and create an empire that would stand the test of time. A true empire was in need of a true capital, and so Grizaka decreed the founding of a grand city bearing her name, Ilzin Grizaka, sitting astride a major tributary of the Sorrow. And at the city’s heart, a mighty fortress was built, called Gnollakaz - Fortress Of The Gnolls.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 4: Gremrabo

Self-aggrandisement was common in many gnollish cultures but the Pyreclaw had made an art form of it. Whether soldier, merchant or priest, nothing was more important to a Pyreclaw gnoll than their reputation. Though prideful and egotistical, the Pyreclaw knew that allowing the killing of rivals over the smallest slights would be disastrous for the pack. As a result, a way of non-violently resolving conflicts emerged within Pyreclaw culture known as the Gremrabo, the "Insult War". The Gremrabo would see two opposing gnolls invent increasingly outlandish insults about their opponent in front of an audience, the first gnoll unable to respond to an insult being declared the loser. The importance of this practice became so respected by the gnolls, that on occasion Kheteratans were able to use Gremrabo to save their towns from an impending raid if they were unable to offer tribute.

Effects: Army morale: +10%; Power projection from insults: +0.5.

Idea 5: Red Sails on the River

Prior to their conquest of the Kheteratan heartlands, Pyreclaw gnolls would regularly sail down the river in heavily armed barges which were notable for their sails depicting the flag of Gnollakaz, a stylised design of The Sorrow running red with blood. These journeys would see them extorting tribute in the form of wealth and slaves from the towns they encountered, sacking those that dared to defy them.

Effects: National tax modifier: +15%.

Idea 6: Blood and Gold

The gold mines of Golkora found infamy throughout Sarhal for the sheer number of slaves that lost their lives within the depths of the mines. For the rulers of Gnollakaz this was a small price to pay, the vast quantities of gold funding their campaigns into Kheterata and purchasing high quality equipment for their warriors. This greater availability also facilitated a growing cultural importance of the precious metal, particular among the upper echelons of society. As the chieftains of the Pyreclaw Gnolls became increasingly settled and integrated into the power structures of the humans they ruled over, demand for elaborate and ostentatious golden jewellery and other fancies grew to fevered heights.

Effects: Yearly inflation reduction: +0.15%.

Idea 7: The Dance of Demons

When Grizaka entered the Pyramid of Elikhet to defile the dead gods corpse, she did not return, but had ensured that her daughter inherited the throne of Gnollakaz safely. She would reign for many years as a stabilising influence. However, upon her death her two daughters, the elder Xukret and the younger Kyztzehr, both attempted to claim the throne. The conflict between the two sisters became known as The Dance of Demons, and saw Gnollakaz ripped apart by a vicious civil war.

Xukret was supported by the Xhazobkult Shamans and the Warlocks of Rakkaz, as well as being loosely allied with Viakkoc who invaded from the northern coast, hoping to destabilise their old foe by tipping the scales in the civil war. By contrast, Kyztzehr was supported by the human population and the Khetist Clergy, as well as eventually the Haraagtsedi to the east. In the end Kyztzehr emerged victorious, marking a significant shift among the Pyreclaw Gnolls towards Kheteratan culture and the declaration of a new Gnollish-Kheteratan realm, Konolkhatep. Had she failed in her bid for the throne, who knows what the fate of Gnollakaz would have been under Xukret and the Xhazobkult…

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Ambition: Gnollakaz Ambition

Effects: Core-creation cost: -10%.
